title: fix(objectql)!: expand and the master-detail parent root never hydrate a stored-metadata-body table
body:
Fixes #24358

Clause-②: no (narrowing) (owes one `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review before the queue)

⚠️ **Security card.** This body keeps to the card's disclosure line: category and position only. No request, field path or value is written here. Tests use synthetic placeholders only.

## What changes

The stored-metadata-body family (`STORED_METADATA_BODY_OBJECTS`) is projected at its doors, but only for the object a request names. Two relationship hydrations in `packages/objectql` read a family row as an ordinary row. Each now refuses a family target with the one family predicate (`isStoredMetadataBodyObject`), as PR #24344 does at the one-hop loader.

- **Exit 1, `expandRelatedRecords`.** A reference into the family is never expanded, at any depth, for any caller. The field keeps its stored id: the answer the door already gives for a reference the caller may not expand (#22661's precedent, and the refused sub-read).
- **Exit 2, the master-detail `parent` root.** `resolveMasterDetailParent` and `resolveMasterDetailParents` never read a family header. `parent` stays unbound, which is the fail-closed signal (#4889) an unreadable header already gives, so a field rule that reads it has no verdict, whatever the row holds. The `validate()` preview's own first header read (`resolvePreviewParents`) gets the same guard, so the preview reads no family row either.
- **The family's enumeration pin** gains both exits (26 → 28 rows), each naming its owning pin.

No second projection. Nothing in `packages/spec`, no new error code, and no edit to the doors' projection or the reader-context seam. `resolveMasterDetailRelation` is unchanged: the refusal sits at the reads, so the relation's other readers keep their answers.

## Reach, measured before the fix

Live over HTTP, on `main` `a2a3777bf` (`app-todo`, SQLite, `--fresh`), with a synthetic stored datasource-type row carrying a placeholder credential, and a control row without one. "Served" means a value the family's own door withholds from that same reader: the credential material or the unkeyed hash. For every reader below, the family's own door served 0 such values.

**Exit 1 (`expand`).** Rows of the carrier that served a family value. Each cell holds for the list read with both expand spellings, the single-record read and the nested query form.

| Reader | Session | API key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Administrator | YES 1/1 | YES 1/1 |
| Member granted read on the family table | YES 1/1 | YES 1/1 |
| Default member (read on the carrier only) | NO 0/1 (stored id) | NO 0/1 (stored id) |

- The MCP tools declare no expand parameter (read in code), so the MCP reader is not an entry point.
- A hook body's `ctx.api` read reaches the same loop through `find`. It is pinned at the engine, not measured over HTTP.

**Exit 2 (the `parent` root).** The verdict for the same write under the header holding the placeholder and under the control header:

| Reader | Verdict depends on the row? |
| --- | --- |
| Administrator | YES: `requiredWhen` 2/2 writes differ; `readonlyWhen` over the stored hash 2/2 differ |
| Member granted read on the family table | YES: `requiredWhen` 2/2 differ |
| Default member | NO: the same unbound refusal under both headers |

Why #24316's dev saw "refused as unbound": the write's first header read is the caller's own read door (#22519, `masterDetailHeadersCallerReads`). For a caller whose door does not return the family header, `parent` stays unbound. For a caller whose door does return it, the second, elevated read binds the whole row.

**Producers.** Each door, for a lookup and for a master_detail into a family table:

- metadata save door: ACCEPTED 1/1 for each;
- `os validate` and `os build`: ACCEPTED, exit 0, for both;
- package install over HTTP: its body refuses inline object definitions (400). An installed artifact's objects arriving by another path: NOT MEASURED.
- In-repo producers declaring such a reference: 0. As a control, references to an ordinary platform table appear in 26 files.

**Exposure.**

- Exit 1: the `expand` loop was first published in `@objectstack/objectql` 3.1.0 (bisected over the npm tarballs). The family's door projection was first published in `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` 17.6.0; from that release on, `expand` bypasses it. The loop has no family check in 17.6.0 and 17.7.0 (`latest`), or in `18.0.0-next.3` (`next`).
- Exit 2: the header binder is published from `@objectstack/objectql` 17.0.0-rc.4 (a symbol bisect; an earlier spelling was not measured). It is unguarded in the same three releases.
- Cloud's framework pin was NOT MEASURED directly: the cloud repository is not reachable from this session. The pin triage read on #24316 (`be076dad28a0`) is on `main`, and its tree carries both exits unguarded beside the door projection.

## After the fix

Live, after rebuilding objectql, on a fresh backend:

- Exit 1: 0 family values served across all 6 reader and auth cells and all 4 read forms. The field answers with the stored id.
- Exit 2: the same refusal under both headers, for all 3 readers.
- Both save doors still accept the field. That is the route decision below.

## Route, by the four axes

The engine guards were chosen. The author-time refusal (a lint rule refusing a reference or master_detail into a family table at save) was not added here.

- **Business need:** 0 in-repo producers declare such a reference, so there is no pull for a new authoring rule.
- **Long-term:** the engine is the one place every producer reaches, including an installed artifact that runs no authoring rule. So the guards are owed under either route.
- **AI error-proofing:** a loud refusal at save would teach the author sooner. The trade-off is recorded for the seat and the maintainer rather than taken here.
- **Startup focus:** a new authoring-rule surface is held back by default.

## Verification (head `b3af029a0`, after merging `origin/main`)

- `@objectstack/objectql` test: 443 files, 8337 passed.
- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` test (before the merge, at `61df76467`): 244 passed and 3 skipped files, 20641 passed and 19 skipped. The family pin was re-run after the merge: 9 passed.
- New engine pin `engine-hydration-stored-metadata-body.test.ts`: 22 passed, with PR #24344's pin beside it (32 together).
- typecheck: objectql exit 0 (its tests are covered by `check:test-typecheck`) and metadata-protocol exit 0 (the pin is in its tsc program).
- `dispatch-gates --commands`: 70 derived, 70 run, each exit captured before any pipe, all 0. `--ran` printed "70 derived, 70 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero)".
- **Ablations** (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`; each mutation landed and was restored to the HEAD blob with `git diff HEAD` empty):
  - expand guard: 8 cases red;
  - single-id header guard: 4 red (the update path);
  - batch header guard: 4 red (the insert path);
  - preview guard: 4 red. Its first attempt was an anchor miss, which the tool refused: nothing was written, and it was re-run with the right anchor.

## Acceptance notes

- The preview guard in `resolvePreviewParents` is outside the claim's named functions. It is the third binder of the same `parent` root, in the same file.
- A detail whose master is a family table and whose field rule reads `parent` now refuses every write. That is the fail-closed answer a default member already got before this change.
- The author-time refusal is left for the seat and the maintainer to weigh. No producer exists today.
